# LOOP-QUEUE — standing work queue for autonomous cloud runs

`protocol v3` · created 2026-07-02 (v1) · v3 2026-07-12 (Fable handoff, Ryan-approved
interactive session) · owner: Ryan Gillon

This file is the coordination bus for the cloud loop system:

- **kalshi-research-loop** (every 3 h since 2026-07-12; was 5 h, Sonnet 5): executes ONE
  milestone from the queue below.
- **kalshi-edge-hunter** (nightly ~04:15 UTC, Opus — added 2026-07-12): the thinking seat.
  Idea generation (Q21-class), adversarial review of the day's findings, probe-prep for
  upcoming gates, and the daily plain-English brief (incl. paper P&L once shadows exist).
  It may add queue items and findings; it NEVER flips a verdict without the two-agent rule.
- **kalshi-collector** (hourly, Haiku): runs `python -m collection.hourly_pass` if it exists;
  nothing else, ever.

**Standing approval.** For a cloud run, executing the topmost eligible queue item under this
protocol IS the approved plan — do not wait for interactive approval (CLAUDE.md's plan-first
rule is satisfied by this file). Everything else in CLAUDE.md binds unchanged, especially:
research + data collection + the sanctioned **paper tier** of `execution/` ONLY (see the
2026-07-12 Stop-rules amendment — demo/live tiers are NOT cloud-runnable), the real-ask bar,
source tags on every persisted price, invariants green before commit.

## Run protocol (research loop)

0a. **History-integrity check (added 2026-07-10, after main was rewound to a 6-day-old
   checkpoint on 2026-07-08 and the loops unknowingly redid a week of work).** Before ANY
   other step: `gh pr list --state merged --limit 5 --json number,mergeCommit`, then for
   each `git merge-base --is-ancestor <mergeCommit.oid> origin/main`. Also verify the
   newest `kb/00-LOG.md` entry date on `origin/main` is not older than the newest
   `tape/*/dt=*` file date by more than 2 days. If EITHER check fails, `main` has been
   rewound or rewritten: do NOT pick queue work, do NOT push anything on top of the rewound
   base. Instead: post a `Priority: max` ntfy note ("main history rewound — needs Ryan"),
   open a GitHub issue titled `main rewound — <date>` with the evidence (which merged PR is
   unreachable, current main SHA), and END THE RUN. Recovery is Ryan-supervised, never
   automatic — see kb/00-LOG.md 2026-07-10 reconciliation entry for the one prior repair.

0. **Claim check (do this before picking work — prevents duplicate runs).** A cloud session
   cannot push straight to `main` (confirmed empirically 2026-07-03: two consecutive runs
   each rebased cleanly, `git push origin main` still fell back to the session's own branch
   with zero rebase conflicts — this is a permission boundary, not a race). So "state of
   `main`" and "state of the queue" can lag behind in-flight work sitting in open PRs.
   `git fetch origin main` and list open PRs targeting `main` in this repo. For each open
   PR: if its title/body names a queue item that is still TODO/IN-PROGRESS here, that item is
   **claimed** — do not redo it. If the PR is green (checks pass) and unmodified for a while,
   merge it yourself (squash) before doing anything else, so `main` catches up; if it's stale
   or broken, note that in the digest and pick the next eligible item instead.
0b. **Stranded-tape sweep (added 2026-07-04, after 10 collector passes silently stranded).**
   The hourly collector's push to `main` fails intermittently and falls back to a
   `tape/hourly-*` branch; that tape never reaches `main` on its own. As part of every
   research run: `git ls-remote --heads origin 'refs/heads/tape/hourly-*' 'refs/heads/tape/burst-*'`
   (`burst-*` added 2026-07-10 — the burst legs below use the same fallback mechanism); for each such
   branch, union-append any JSONL lines missing from `main`'s per-day tape files into your
   run's own commit (line-level dedupe is safe — tape is append-only JSONL with unique
   capture identity per line; never rewrite or reorder existing lines), then, only after
   your PR containing those lines has merged, delete the swept branch. Skip any branch
   whose commit is younger than 30 minutes (may still be mid-run).

1. Read `CLAUDE.md`, this file, `kb/strategies/00-index.md` — from `main` HEAD, post claim-check.
2. Env: `pip install -e ".[dev,analysis]"` (venv optional in a throwaway sandbox).
3. Pick the TOPMOST unclaimed item whose status is TODO or IN-PROGRESS (skip DONE / BLOCKED /
   DEAD / claimed-by-an-open-PR). Do ONE milestone (~one focused stage). If the item blocks
   mid-run, set its status to `BLOCKED(<reason>)` and move to the next eligible item.
   **(v3, 2026-07-12) Idle-run policy:** if NO item is eligible, the run is an IDLE RUN and
   must still produce one unit of real work, chosen in this order: (a) convert an UNENFORCED
   lesson from `kb/lessons/00-lessons.md` into an invariant/test; (b) write + offline-test
   the probe script for the NEXT time-gated queue item so it fires the day its gate opens;
   (c) a data-quality deep-dive on one tape family (gaps, drift, join-ability — one finding);
   (d) idea-gen prep for Q21 (observations memo from accumulated tape, no registration).
   The step-0b sweep still runs, but "sweep only" is no longer a valid run outcome.
4. Gates before ANY commit: `pytest` green AND `python scripts/invariants.py --full` green.
   **(L162, 2026-07-25) Fresh-gate-line rule:** any pytest/invariants count quoted in a
   finding, `kb/00-LOG.md` entry, or "Log of runs" line must be taken AFTER the commit's
   last code change — never a mid-edit snapshot presented as final (L162 caught a run
   whose quoted "1743 collected / 14 tests" had drifted to 1750/21 by the time the tree
   actually landed). If re-running the exact count right before commit isn't practical,
   state it as a floor ("≥N collected, 0 failed") instead of a fixed number.
5. Bookkeeping: update the item's Status line in this file; append one dated entry to
   `kb/00-LOG.md` (match its existing format); findings → `findings/`; strategy status
   changes → `kb/strategies/00-index.md`; append one line to "Log of runs" below.
   **(v3, 2026-07-12) Two-agent verdict rule (codifies what the S10/S6 verdicts already
   practiced):** any verdict-class change — a registry status flip, a bootstrap CI destined
   for `kb/`/`findings/`, a kill decision — requires TWO agents: the producer (edge-prober
   or main context) AND an independent `verifier` re-run that CONFIRMS before commit. A
   verdict without verifier confirmation may only be committed as `PROVISIONAL` and must not
   flip the registry. (Fable's oversight is gone; redundancy replaces it.)
6. Git: commit (message conventions from history: `build:` / `probe(Sx):` / `tape:` /
   `docs:`) on your own branch, push it, then open a PR against `main` (`gh`/GitHub MCP —
   do NOT attempt `git push origin main`, it will not succeed from a cloud session). If gates
   (step 4) are green and the diff is research/data/paper-tier-only — no execution code
   outside `execution/`'s sanctioned paper tier (2026-07-12 Stop-rules amendment), no
   demo/live order paths, no credential handling (Stop rules forbid these, so this is a
   re-check, not a new bar) — **merge the PR immediately** (squash) so `main` is current for the next firing. If
   gates are red or the milestone is only partially done, leave the PR open with an
   IN-PROGRESS note in its body and say so in the digest; do not merge broken or incomplete
   work into `main`.
7. Final message must be EXACTLY this shape — it is Ryan's phone digest:

   ```
   RUN DIGEST
   - Done: <one line>
   - Found: <key numbers; any price carries its price_source_tag>
   - Next: <one line>
   - Repo: <short sha> → <branch> (PR #<n>, merged|open)
   ```

8. Phone note (all legs — research loop, cloud collector, VPS collector, weekly retro, burst
   legs; added 2026-07-03). Best-effort, never blocks a run: POST one plain-English summary a
   non-programmer understands (no jargon, SHAs, or ticker codes) to the leg's ntfy URL
   (supplied privately per the 2026-07-10 topic migration in (e) below; formerly the URL in
   `config/notify.topic`) via `curl -s -m 10 -H 'Title: <leg name>' -d '<text>'`. Hourly
   collector notes use `-H 'Priority: low'` (silent feed); anything failed or needing Ryan's
   action uses `-H 'Priority: high'`. Ryan reads this feed on his phone via the ntfy app —
   it is the human window into the loop; write for him, not for the log.
   **Hardening (2026-07-10, after the feed went silent for 2 days without anyone noticing):**
   (a) the note is mandatory on EVERY research-loop run, including idle/maintenance runs and
   runs that end early on a guard (step 0a) or a blocked queue — silence is never a valid
   outcome; (b) any run that fails its gates, loses its push, or hits step 0a posts at
   `Priority: high` or above; (c) if the ntfy POST itself fails, say so in the run digest so
   the retro can see the notification pipe is broken; (d) the weekly retro's review MUST
   include "did phone notes flow every day this week?" as a checklist item.
   **(e) Topic migration (2026-07-10, Ryan-approved public-repo hardening):** the ntfy topic
   is no longer stored in this repo. The repo went public on 2026-07-10 and ntfy.sh topics
   are world-readable AND world-writable — a committed topic name lets anyone inject
   priority-5 messages that the `ntfy-watch` responder would investigate. Each cloud leg's
   routine prompt now carries the URL directly (private to Ryan's account); the VPS leg reads
   `NTFY_TOPIC_URL` from `/root/.secrets/kalshi-headless.env`; Ryan's local sessions read
   `~/.claude/secrets/kalshi-ntfy-topic`. `config/notify.topic` holds only the OLD, retired
   topic as a temporary fallback until the VPS is flipped, after which it gets deleted —
   nothing reads it for action anymore (`ntfy-watch` polls the new topic only). NEVER commit
   the new topic name to any file in this repo, any PR, or any run's final message.

9. **Paper sub-pass (v3, 2026-07-12).** If `execution/strategy_api.SHADOW_REGISTRY` is
   non-empty: advance `execution/paper_broker.PaperBroker` over tape appended since the
   ledger's last entry (deterministic replay — same tape, same ledger, same state), append
   the resulting ledger lines under `paper/` in your commit, and include the broker's
   one-line `daily_summary()` in the run digest and the phone note. An empty registry makes
   this step a silent no-op. Paper results are evidence, not verdicts: a shadow's track
   record feeds the live-gate criteria (Stop rules amendment) but never flips a registry
   status by itself.

## Stop rules (non-negotiable)

- NEVER touch credentials, never place a trade. Capital requires an in-person sign-off from
  Ryan that no cloud run can obtain — by design.
  **Amendment (2026-07-12, Ryan-approved interactive session — the paper-harness decision):**
  "never write order/execution code" is replaced by a three-tier lane under `execution/`:
  - **paper** — pure simulation over committed tape; no order ever leaves the process; no
    network calls. Cloud runs MAY build, extend, and run it. Every paper fill carries
    `fill_model` + `price_source_tag` (a fill against a `synthetic` price is forbidden);
    the ledger is append-only JSONL under `paper/`, committed like tape.
  - **demo** — Kalshi demo-API orders. VPS/local only; NOT cloud-runnable. Not built yet.
  - **live** — real orders. Requires ALL of: (1) block-bootstrapped real-ask CI > 0,
    (2) ≥14 days of shadow-paper track record consistent with the backtest, (3) a
    per-strategy `LIVE-AUTH.md` signed by Ryan in person, (4) a bankroll cap + kill switch
    from `execution/limits.py` (the single sanctioned caps site), (5) credentials that exist
    ONLY on the VPS/local — cloud sandboxes never receive them. Authenticated/order
    endpoints may exist ONLY in `execution/kalshi_client.py` (unbuilt until graduation is
    near). Live trading therefore stays structurally impossible for autonomous cloud runs.
- An edge is "proven" ONLY by a block-bootstrapped 95% CI strictly > 0 at `real_ask` prices
  net of fees. A DEAD verdict is a success — record it honestly and move on.
- Never relax an invariant, never delete or reorder queue items; append, don't rewrite.
- Timebox: if a milestone isn't converging, commit honest partial state with an
  IN-PROGRESS note rather than forcing a result.

## Subagent roster (added 2026-07-06, ops — Ryan-requested)

`.claude/agents/` now defines a project agent team: an **Opus lead on high reasoning**
(`research-lead` — plans, decomposes, reviews; never edits files itself; was Fable-class
until Fable's retirement 2026-07-12) guiding five
**Opus workers** — `collector-engineer` (build collectors + tests), `edge-prober` (probes/
backtests/bootstraps, one falsifiable milestone each), `verifier` (adversarial skeptic:
re-runs and attacks every number before it enters kb/ or findings/), `kb-distiller`
(compounds lessons into `kb/lessons/00-lessons.md` and escalates UNENFORCED lessons into
invariants/tests), and `tape-auditor` (read-only tape health/coverage/stranded-branch
reports). Each agent's charter carries the Stop rules and the real-ask bar; none can place
orders or touch credentials by charter, and the repo Stop rules bind regardless.

Loop usage: a research run MAY delegate its milestone through `research-lead` (which fans
out to the workers) instead of doing everything in the main context — the run protocol
above (claim-check, step-0b sweep, gates, bookkeeping, digest) binds identically either
way. Two standing quality rules regardless of who executes: (1) any number destined for
`kb/` or `findings/` passes the `verifier` bar — re-runnable, provenance-tagged,
statistically honest; (2) every run that learned something ends with a `kb-distiller`-style
ledger append, so knowledge compounds instead of evaporating between stateless runs. The
lessons ledger lives at `kb/lessons/00-lessons.md`; its UNENFORCED rows are a standing
work queue any idle run may draw from (converting a lesson into an invariant/test is
always an eligible milestone, no queue item needed).

## Burst-capture legs (added 2026-07-10 — Ryan-approved, interactive session)

The S9 lead-lag resolution (`findings/2026-07-06-polymarket-leadlag-s9-resolution.md`)
identified sub-hourly event-window captures as a new automation class that needed Ryan's
sign-off; that sign-off was given 2026-07-10. Five ONE-SHOT cloud triggers now exist
(created via the trigger API — they live in Ryan's account, not this file):

| trigger | event | window (UTC) | families / interval |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kalshi-burst-cpi-0714` | June CPI print (12:30Z release) | Jul 14 12:05→13:45 | econ,cpi,fed,crypto @60s |
| `kalshi-burst-wcsemi1-0714` | WC semifinal 1 (19:00Z kickoff) | Jul 14 20:10→22:30 | wc @120s |
| `kalshi-burst-wcsemi2-0715` | WC semifinal 2 (19:00Z kickoff) | Jul 15 20:10→22:30 | wc @120s |
| `kalshi-burst-wcfinal-0719` | WC FINAL (19:00Z kickoff) | Jul 19 20:10→22:45 | wc @120s |
| `kalshi-burst-fomc-0729` | FOMC decision (18:00Z statement) | Jul 29 17:40→19:45 | fed,econ,crypto @90s |

Each runs `python -m collection.burst_capture --until <end> --interval <s> --families <list>`
— a thin loop over the existing collectors' one-pass functions (no new tape family, no schema
change; burst lines are distinguishable downstream purely by `fetch_ts` density), commits
tape ONLY (`tape: burst <slug> <ts>`, fallback branch `tape/burst-*`, swept by step 0b),
posts a step-8 phone note, and carries a hard date guard so the cron's annual re-fire is a
no-op. Burst runs obey every Stop rule: they collect, they never analyze, never trade. The
point: this is exactly the data class whose absence killed S9's lead-lag test — S17's
lead-lag question (who reprices first around a macro shock, Kalshi or Polymarket?) becomes
testable on this tape. After each event the trigger should be disabled/deleted (weekly retro
or Ryan); a fired one-shot left enabled is harmless but untidy.

## Regime change — Polymarket is now a TRADEABLE venue (2026-07-15, Ryan interactive session)

Until now Polymarket was a **data source only** — S9 lead-lag, S17 macro pairs, and S20 wallet
forensics all READ Polymarket, but every cross-venue divergence was basis risk because only the
Kalshi leg was ever fillable. Ryan now has a funded, order-capable Polymarket account, so
cross-venue and Polymarket-native edges are ACTIONABLE for the first time. Three facts the loop
MUST bake in (researched 2026-07-15, sources below) — do NOT carry the stale "Polymarket = zero
fees" assumption any longer:

1. **Polymarket now charges fees (Fee Structure V2, eff. ~2026-03-30).** Taker-only, makers get a
   rebate; the formula is `fee = C × rate × p × (1−p)` — the SAME shape as
   `core.pricing.fee_per_contract` (Kalshi's 0.07). Rates: **Polymarket US ≈ 0.05 taker** (cap
   ~$1.25 / 100 contracts @ 50¢, maker rebate ~−0.0125); international **crypto 0.07 / sports
   0.03–0.05**, geopolitics fee-free. → any cross-venue arb must charge BOTH legs' real fees; the
   "one free leg" premise is DEAD. When modeling the Polymarket leg, ADD a `POLYMARKET_*_RATE`
   constant to `core/pricing.py` (the ONLY sanctioned fee-coefficient site —
   `scripts/invariants.py::no_handrolled_fee_rate` statically forbids hand-rolled rates elsewhere);
   do NOT hardcode `0.05` in a probe script.
2. **The legal US venue is Polymarket US (QCX/QCEX, CFTC-regulated DCM/DCO, fiat-funded)** — a
   DIFFERENT venue from the international USDC/Polygon CLOB. Our `polymarket_pairs` /
   `polymarket_macro_pairs` tape is captured off `clob.polymarket.com/book` = the INTERNATIONAL
   book. So the prices Ryan can actually fill (Polymarket US) may differ in level and liquidity
   from our tape. Every cross-venue finding MUST carry this provenance caveat: our Polymarket leg
   is `real_ask` on the international book, NOT a Polymarket-US fill.
3. **Resolution basis is now a capital risk, not a footnote.** Polymarket international resolves via
   the UMA optimistic oracle (proposer bond ~$750, ~2h challenge window, DVM token-holder vote
   escalation over days, documented ambiguous/controversial resolutions); Kalshi resolves centrally
   by rulebook + named source agency. "Same question" on the two venues can resolve DIFFERENTLY, so
   a cross-venue position is an arb ONLY if the two contracts are resolution-equivalent — otherwise
   it is a naked directional bet. The `polymarket_pairs` collector's existing refusal to force a
   match (`unmatched`/`ambiguous`, never guessed) now protects capital, not just data quality.

Sources (researched 2026-07-15): Polymarket help "Trading Fees" (help.polymarket.com/en/articles/
13364478); Sacra & Galaxy fee breakdowns (V2 eff. 2026-03-30; US venue eff. 2026-04-03); UMA
resolution mechanics (crowdtells, turbinefi); QCX/QCEX CFTC acquisition (US News, Sacra, 2025–26).

**Loop boundary (unchanged Stop rules).** Cloud loops CANNOT act on this — trading Polymarket needs
a sanctioned `execution/polymarket_client.py` + the paper→demo→live gate + Ryan-side credentials.
What the loop CAN do is the read-only tradeability RESEARCH below (Q31/Q32, paper-tier only) and the
offline-tested collector code for Q33 (which self-activates only when Ryan's credential appears).

consuming the modal 1–2¢ two-sided spread before adverse selection is even charged — the same
fee-floor mechanism that killed S13. Adversarially reviewed and **CONFIRMED** by the `verifier`
subagent: independently reproduced every number exactly, swept additional thresholds
(≤15/20/25/30¢) trying to find an alive population, confirmed the only CI>0 cut (≤30¢
frozen-inclusive, +$0.00229) fails lesson L27's magnitude-vs-tick gate and is itself a wing
artifact — under the honest movement-conditioned cut every threshold tested is strictly
negative. More days of the SAME hourly-cadence tape will not resurrect this (structural, not
sample-size). `kb-distiller` subagent compounded: `kb/strategies/00-index.md` S6 flipped
`data-collecting → dead ✗`; 3 lessons appended (L30 flat-maker-fee, L31 wing-spread artifact,

sharp-odds anchor this run doesn't have (same key gap as Q1).

Status: DONE (2026-07-13, research loop) — **anatomy only, no registry flip** (per this item's

tests) decomposed the overround over 629 crypto_hourly snapshots (KXBTC 316/KXETH 313, 172
settled event-hours each): **97.4% (BTC) / 84.3% (ETH) of the overround sits in wings**, split
between 1¢-floor pins AND stale one-sided `wing_elevated` asks (on BTC the latter, $2.17,
actually exceeds the floor pins, $1.71 — a second artifact component L12 didn't name). Depth
join (`tape/orderbook_depth/`, 328/629 snapshots join-eligible) **REFUTES "wings are quote-only"**
— floor wings rest median 22,768 (BTC) / 36,253 (ETH) contracts; they carry no edge because the
flat $0.01 maker fee eats a 1¢ ask (L30), not from lack of size. Active-band
`Σyes_ask − 1 − maker_fees`, block-bootstrapped by event-hour (n=172, 10k resamples): **BTC
+0.0087 CI [−0.0036, +0.0215] — fails the magnitude gate, no edge**; **ETH +0.1271 CI
[+0.1046, +0.1523] — statistically positive but EXPLORATORY**, deferred to S14's existing
queue-aware fill-sim gate (the active-band mids themselves sum >1.0, a heuristic tell — not a
theorem — that this is nominal ask-width in a thin book, per the verifier's decomposition). S14
parameter block emitted (band width, quote prices, nominal expected capture), tagged unproven.
Verifier re-derived every load-bearing number independently (exact match) and instrumented the
join staleness (p99 34.8s, max 165.6s — sound); one causal wording (ETH mid-sum attribution) was
corrected per the verifier's caveat before commit. See
`findings/2026-07-13-btc-ladder-overround-anatomy-q20.md`. 664 tests green (642 prior + 22),
`invariants --full` green.

### Q28 — S24: Near-close hourly-return overreaction fade on two-sided sports books
Status: DONE (2026-07-14, research loop) — **verdict DEAD by round-trip, verifier-CONFIRMED.**
`scripts/q28_s24_nearclose_fade_probe.py` (+13 offline tests) block-bootstraps a real_ask-entry/

S24 flipped idea → dead ✗. Still 0 proven edges. See `findings/2026-07-14-nearclose-fade-s24-verdict.md`.
Mechanism (Theme 7 behavioral, De Bondt-Thaler/Tetlock): an hourly-scale near-close mid jump in a two-sided
sports book (retail overreacting to the last salient in-game event) partially reverses over the next hour;
fade the jump. Losing counterparty = the overreacting retail flow. Distinct from S18 (elections/polls,
idea-stage) — different category and horizon. Data (already-collected): `tape/orderbook_depth/` price paths
in the Q25 high-turnover cells. Milestone (one read-only probe): identify consecutive-snapshot mid jumps
≥ X¢ in the near-close window; enter a fade at real_ask against the jump; measure the next-snapshot
reversal; block-bootstrap by distinct GAME (L6). Binding gates (verifier-mandated, do NOT weaken) — the
first is load-bearing for distinctness: (1) the EXIT must be explicitly specified and the CI must charge
the FULL realized round-trip (both taker legs: 2× 0.07 fee + 2× half-spread ≈ a 6-8¢ hurdle on a ~3.7¢-
overround two-sided book) — AND if the only profitable exit is hold-to-settlement, S24 collapses into S22's
mechanism (a directional settlement bet keyed on a recent jump) and MUST be routed to S22's slot, NOT
double-counted; (2) the ≥X¢ jump threshold must clear the frozen-BBO/bid-ask-bounce noise floor (Q25:
58-94% frozen — a real mid move, not a one-tick flicker); (3) bootstrap by distinct GAME, ≥10 games —
verify the jump population reaches the floor (Q25's sub-hour buckets are mostly insufficient); (4)
momentum-vs-reversal is a sign question so the opposing-sign cluster (L41) is NOT guaranteed — assert
`bootstrap_verdict_admissible` admissible and `clears_tick_magnitude`. Kill: jumps continue (momentum, not
reversal) / reversal < round-trip cost / hourly cadence too coarse (S9-family) / CI fails either gate.
Honest expectation: DEAD-by-round-trip is likely; sound and novel nonetheless.

Mechanism: in the post-close window (game over, market not yet auto-settled/purged) Kalshi sports books linger with real two-sided depth (Q25: baseball post_close n=2,478, median ask-queue 25,884, 16% turnover, only 4% any-empty). A taker who knows the public game result lifts a winner-side YES still offered below ~$0.98 (or shorts the decided loser), collecting the near-certain $1 net of taker fee. Losing counterparty = stale limit orders / market-makers that haven't pulled quotes, or bettors unaware the game ended. NOT the S1/S5/S7 taker-into-overround death: a decided outcome carries NO probabilistic overround (one side worth $1, other $0). NOT the S10 no-fillable-price death: sports post_close is two-sided (4% any-empty vs crypto 96-100%), so a sub-$1 winner ask can genuinely rest and be lifted. Data (already-collected/free): tape/orderbook_depth/ post_close captures (real_ask and real_bid) + realized settlement ex-post from Kalshi's free settled endpoint (collection/sports_history.py::fetch_kalshi_settled, L50, within L11 retention; cache to tape/q29_settlement_cache/). No burst tape, no odds key. Milestone (one read-only probe): over lookahead-clean post_close captures, measure the distribution of (settlement_value minus best fillable winner-side real_ask) net of the 0.07 taker fee (core.pricing); block-bootstrap by GAME (L6). Binding gates (verifier-mandated, do NOT weaken): (1) LOOKAHEAD is load-bearing — entry may use ONLY info public at capture time; restrict to ttc past a margin that provably exceeds the Q25-documented sports-HHMM tz uncertainty (league-local, up to ~13h) PLUS max game duration, and EXCLUDE date-only/coarse-resolution tickers (23:59 UTC clamp, intra-day close unknowable); kill if the lookahead-clean hour-resolved population is under 10 games; (2) FILLABILITY vs mirror artifact — the traded price must be a genuine resting real_ask with real size on the traded side, NOT the one-sided 1¢-floor mirror (buying NO at a mirrored $1.00 is the S10 non-price, L26/L31); assert depth on the traded side; (3) exclude postponed/rescheduled/voided/corrected games (sanity-check result against retention_available) and apply the L52 scalar-result filter; (4) route any CI through core.bootstrap.bootstrap_verdict_admissible (>=10 units, >=1 opposing-sign cluster) AND clears_tick_magnitude (L41/L27) vs the taker fee. Kill: post_close winner-side asks essentially all converged at or above ~$0.98 (no fillable room — likely, Kalshi auto-settles fast) / lookahead-clean population below floor / mirror-artifact non-price / CI fails either gate. Honest expectation: probably DEAD by convergence — a cheap, clean-kill settlement/close-time-mechanics probe that closes a settlement-lag question nobody has tested; the two-agent verdict rule applies to any kill/CI.

### Q31 — Cross-venue tradeability backtest (Kalshi↔Polymarket, real two-legged asks net of BOTH fee models)
Status: DONE (2026-07-16, research loop) — **verdict DEAD, verifier-CONFIRMED, registered S34.** Only the Polymarket-YES + Kalshi-NO direction is testable (Polymarket's NO-token book is never captured — a real tape-coverage gap, not an excuse). 13,158 snapshots / 63 matched pairs (WC-round + Fed-decision; CPI excluded, synthetic leg): block-bootstrap-by-pair mean −$0.0340, 95% CI [−0.0417,−0.0268] ⊄ >0, 0/63 pairs positive, inadmissible/fails tick-magnitude. Robust to a Polymarket-fee-free sensitivity and to the L32 movement-conditioned cut. Fillable-snapshot frequency 2.0%; persistence collapses 84.2%→34.9% once conditioned on the book actually moving (frozen-quote artifact, not a re-offered arb). New `core.pricing.polymarket_fee_per_contract`/`POLYMARKET_US_TAKER_RATE`. Confirms the S9 parity prior now that both legs cost a fee. See `findings/2026-07-16-q31-cross-venue-arb-verdict.md`.
Mechanism: previously untradeable — we could SEE a Kalshi↔Polymarket price divergence but only fill the Kalshi leg, so every gap was basis risk (S9). Ryan can now trade BOTH legs. A true cross-venue arb: buy YES on the cheaper venue + buy the mirror (NO) on the dearer, locking a $1 payout if BOTH legs resolve identically, for a cost < $1 net of both venues' fees. Prior to beat (already measured — S9 first cut, 2026-07-04): the two venues quote nearly the same price, mean gap **+0.20¢**, range −3¢/+3¢ across 48/48 matched WC-round markets — so steady-state parity arb is thin; the edge, if any, lives in TRANSIENT dislocations. Data (already-collected/free): tape/polymarket_pairs/ (WC-round Yes/No, both legs `real_ask` off the live books) + tape/polymarket_macro_pairs/ (Fed-decision + CPI ladders, S17 shape; ~13k lines, current through today). Both carry bitemporal captured_at, so dislocation persistence is measurable at collection cadence. Milestone (one read-only backtest): for every time-aligned matched pair, compute the two-legged cost to lock $1 = (cheaper-venue YES ask) + (dearer-venue NO ask), net of BOTH fee models — Kalshi via core.pricing.fee_per_contract, Polymarket via a NEW core/pricing.py Polymarket rate constant (regime note item 1 — do NOT hand-roll, it trips no_handrolled_fee_rate). Report: how OFTEN net cost < $1 (a fillable arb), the DISTRIBUTION of the gross edge, and how PERSISTENT each dislocation is across consecutive captures (does it survive to the next snapshot — i.e. fillable in time?). Binding gates (do NOT weaken): (1) RESOLUTION-EQUIVALENCE is load-bearing — include a pair ONLY if the two contracts resolve on structurally identical criteria/source/timing; the UMA-vs-Kalshi difference (regime note item 3) makes a non-equivalent pair a directional bet, not an arb — exclude it, count it honestly, never assume equivalence; (2) PROVENANCE — our Polymarket leg is `real_ask` on the INTERNATIONAL book, NOT a Polymarket-US fill (regime note item 2); state this on every number, do NOT claim it as Ryan's realizable fill; (3) both legs must be a genuine resting real_ask with size, not a last/mid reference (polymarket_pairs already refuses `outcomePrices` — keep that); (4) capital/settlement friction is real (two separate pools, USDC bridging $5–30 or fiat rails) — a "fillable arb" that needs instant cross-venue rebalancing is not free; note it, don't model it away; (5) any positivity claim is a `real_ask` cross-venue edge — route a by-pair block-bootstrap through core.bootstrap.bootstrap_verdict_admissible + clears_tick_magnitude before it enters kb/findings; two-agent verdict rule applies. Kill: net two-legged cost ≥ $1 for essentially all resolution-equivalent pairs (parity holds, fees + the tight gap kill it — LIKELY given the +0.20¢ prior) / dislocations never persist to the next capture (unfillable at cadence — the S9 lead-lag death in a new guise) / resolution-equivalent population below the bootstrap floor. Honest expectation: probably DEAD — the S9 parity prior is tight and fees now bite BOTH legs — but this is the cheapest way to decide the whole cross-venue thesis before any execution code is built, and a clean kill retires it.

### Q34 — S14 queue-model fill-realism revalidation (EV-protecting — pin the real base before any rebate multiplier)
Status: DONE (2026-07-16, research loop) — **verdict DEAD, verifier-CONFIRMED, S14 flips `data-collecting` → `dead ✗`.** `scripts/s14_queue_fillsim.py` replaced the candle-through fill proxy (L39) with a price-time-priority queue-aware fill model over `tape/orderbook_depth/` `no_bids` (executed volume from the already-committed `tape/s14_ladder_fillsim/` candle cache, read offline, no re-fetch). Result FALSIFIES the Q13 candle-proxy headline (+$0.0925 CI [+0.063,+0.123]): queue-aware block-boot by event-hour mean **−$0.0453, 95% CI [−0.0809,−0.0121]** (fully below zero), n=146 event-hours, `bootstrap_verdict_admissible` PASS (54 opposing/92 losing) / `clears_tick_magnitude` FAIL. Overall fill rate 27.18% (582/2141) ≫ the S19 0.45% floor → dies on the EDGE not adequacy. Winner-payout leg (the $1 catastrophic loss) fully in the P&L for every measurable event-hour, never conditioned away — 290 event-hours dropped on winner-leg measurability only (verifier-confirmed conservative: zeroing them instead still gives −$0.0152). **This closes the repo's last non-DEAD candidate — still 0 proven edges.** Two-agent trail: edge-prober built+ran, verifier independently reproduced (seed=42) and CONFIRMED before the registry flip. New lessons L85 (candle-through fill proxies are presumptively verdict-invalidating for any small-net-of-two-large-legs P&L — the S13/S19/S21/S23/S14 purge is now complete) and L86 (winner/catastrophic-leg measurability asymmetry: drop the unit, never zero the loss, verify the drop is conservative). Q35's rebate-multiplier BUILD half for S14 specifically does not unlock (S14 is dead); Q35's Milestone A analysis over S13/S19/S21/S23/S29 is untouched by this verdict and remains separately eligible. `execution/strategy_api.SHADOW_REGISTRY` still carries `s14_ladder_underwriting` (the OLD candle-proxy paper strategy) — flagged for Ryan: continuing to paper-trade a now-DEAD-at-real-fills strategy is harmless (paper tier, no capital) but not decision-useful; deregistering it is a judgment call left for Ryan/a future run rather than made unilaterally here. See `findings/2026-07-16-q34-s14-queue-fillsim-verdict.md`.
Mechanism/why: S14 (ladder-underwriting — rest maker offers to sell overpriced longshot wing brackets on hourly crypto ladders, collect premium) is the repo's ONLY positive-proxy edge (+$0.0925/contract proxy; paper +$5.77 net over 214 fills, gross +$7.91). But EVERY S14 paper fill is tagged `fill_model: maker_candle_through` with caveats `no_queue_model` + `optimistic_fill` — the EXACT biased proxy that killed S13 (L39: candle-fill assumed ~94% fills; real queue fill was 0.45%; Q24 median queue-ahead 485 contracts). So S14's +$5.77 is very likely OVERSTATED and its edge is UNPROVEN at real queue fills. Milestone (one read-only probe): build a queue-aware fill-sim for S14's resting wing offers over `tape/orderbook_depth/` (or the crypto bracket depth tape) — model queue position (size-ahead at the resting price), recompute the HONEST fill rate and net edge net of the flat 1¢ maker fee (`core.pricing`, L30), block-bootstrap by EVENT/hour (L6). Binding gates (do NOT weaken): (1) queue-aware, NOT candle-through (L39) — kill if fill rate ≤ the S19 0.45% floor; (2) the catastrophic wing-hits-in-the-money leg fully in the P&L, never conditioned away (L41/G2); (3) route the CI through `bootstrap_verdict_admissible` + `clears_tick_magnitude` (L27/L41); two-agent verifier rule. Kill: real queue fill collapses the edge like S13/S19 → S14 flips positive-proxy → DEAD-at-real-fills, closing the whole ladder-underwriting / short-the-overpriced-tail factor family. Survive: S14 becomes the FIRST edge with a real (not proxy) positive number — and ONLY THEN is Q35's rebate multiplier worth building. Honest expectation: uncertain — the candle-proxy has been the killer every prior time (S13/S19), so DEAD-at-real-fills is the base rate; but S14 has cleared every gate so far, so it earns the honest queue-model test. This is EV-PROTECTING: it stops a false-positive from ever reaching capital.

### Q35 — Maker-rebate reframe: re-test the fee-killed maker family on a rebate venue (analysis NOW, build gated)
Status: ANALYSIS HALF DONE (2026-07-16, research loop) — **2/5 flip to a fee-line CI-positive candidate; no registry change.** `scripts/q35_maker_rebate_reframe.py` (+10 offline tests) re-ran S13/S19/S21/S23/S29's own simulate functions over committed tape/cache and swapped the Kalshi maker fee for a flat +0.5¢/+1.25¢ rebate. **S13 flips both scenarios** (mechanical: bid=fair−1¢ by construction, CI [-0.0002,+0.0004]→[+0.0148,+0.0154]→[+0.0223,+0.0229]). **S21/S19 stay dead** (data-adequacy: 0 fills / n=2 event-hours). **S23 stays dead** (lost by more than the fee, mean −4.04¢). **S29 flips only at +1.25¢** (two-sided-book cut, n=119 games, CI [-0.0065,+0.1564]→[+0.0085,+0.1714] fails tick gate→[+0.0160,+0.1789] clears). Two-agent trail: verifier round 1 **REFUTED** the first cut — `collect_s29` had fed the raw disowned earliest-entry population (n=157, the "only S13 flips" headline) instead of the two-sided-book cut the S29 finding's own DEAD verdict rests on; fixed, verifier round 2 **CONFIRMED** (numbers reproduce to 4 decimals). Every flip is a Milestone-B CANDIDATE only (portability/resolution-basis/real-fill bar still owed), never a proven edge. BUILD half remains BLOCKED(polymarket-collector). See `findings/2026-07-16-q35-maker-rebate-reframe-milestone-a.md`.
Status (history): TODO for the ANALYSIS half (read-only, no Polymarket data needed); BLOCKED(polymarket-collector) for the BUILD half. Added 2026-07-15, Ryan interactive session — EV-lever follow-up.
Mechanism/why: S13, S19, S21, S23, S29 all died PARTLY on Kalshi's flat ~1¢ maker fee (L30 fee-death) — a resting maker bid/offer whose margin was thinner than the fee. Those deaths are KALSHI-FEE-SPECIFIC. Polymarket PAYS makers a REBATE (~+1.25¢/contract US venue; int'l 15–20% of the taker pool), so the fee line flips from a cost to income. Quantified on S14's 214 actual paper fills (2026-07-15): fee line swings −$2.14 → +$2.68 (a +$4.81 swing), net +$5.77 → +$10.58 (~2×) — the fee is **27% of S14's gross**, so on thin maker edges the fee line IS the margin. Milestone A (analysis, runnable NOW, read-only over existing findings/tape, NO Polymarket data): for each DEAD maker verdict (S13/S19/S21/S23/S29), re-derive its CI swapping the Kalshi 1¢ maker fee for the Polymarket maker rebate (test a conservative +0.5¢ AND the +1.25¢ US-venue figure). Report which, if any, flip from DEAD to CI-positive ON THE FEE LINE ALONE. Milestone B (BUILD, gated on the Polymarket game-level/crypto collector — Q33-class): any candidate that flips becomes a Polymarket maker-strategy candidate, but must clear (1) PORTABILITY (Polymarket's market shape must actually host the strategy — e.g. S14's fine wing brackets may not exist on Polymarket's coarser up/down crypto markets); (2) RESOLUTION BASIS (Polymarket crypto settles Chainlink/Pyth ≠ Kalshi index — a parallel contract, its own validation); (3) the FULL real-ask/real-fill bar on the ACTUAL venue (a fee-line CI flip is a CANDIDATE, never a proven edge). Binding notes: the rebate is INDICATIVE not exact (pool-funded, varies with volume); a strategy that lost by MORE than the rebate swing stays dead — only sub-~2¢ fee-line losers are in scope; a flipped CI still owes the two-agent verifier rule and `clears_tick_magnitude`. Honest expectation: most stay dead (they lost by more than the rebate); but the check is cheap and read-only, and any sub-2¢ loser re-opens on a rebate venue. This is the single biggest STRUCTURAL EV lever found 2026-07-15 — it does not require a new edge, it changes the SIGN of the fee on every maker fill.

Scope, one deliverable: `scripts/tape_gap_monitor.py` (+ `tests/test_tape_gap_monitor.py`, offline over fixture tape) that aggregates, per tape family per UTC day, (a) the `completeness_ok` signal and (b) "age since last successful pass" (wall-clock gap to the newest `dt=*` line), and emits a per-family health table + a machine-readable JSON. It POSTs a `Priority: high` ntfy note (step-8 mechanism, URL supplied privately to the leg — never in-repo) when any family goes **>2 expected passes silent**, i.e. detector latency ≤6h vs today's unbounded human-only latency. **Hard acceptance (falsifiable), run over the CURRENT committed tape — TWO true-positives it must flag AND one false-positive it must NOT:** (1) flag the 2026-07-09 systemic full-day outage (all families silent at once); (2) flag the 2026-07-15 interior under-capture (~16 dropped passes mid-day despite a full-day span); (3) must **NOT** hard-alert the `polymarket_pairs` silence after 07-15 — triaged 2026-07-16 (HIGH confidence) as BENIGN market-universe exhaustion: the World Cup champion market resolved 07-15 (tape shows `yes_ask=1.0`), so `run()`'s `status=open` discovery correctly returns 0 and its `if lines:` guard (`collection/polymarket_pairs.py:342`) writes no file — a legitimate zero-match, not a pipe break. The detector MUST distinguish "silent because the market universe legitimately emptied / settled" from "silent because the collector crashed or the pass dropped"; a monitor that pages Ryan every time a seasonal family (WC, a resolved event series) ages out is worse than none. Design note: the cleanest disambiguator is a **zero-match heartbeat** — have the empty-match path still emit a status/summary line (the triage's suggested enhancement) so "ran, matched 0, universe empty" is distinguishable in-tape from "did not run." Reads only committed tape + the hourly-pass summary shape; makes no strategy claim. **Ryan pause point (NOT crossed by the build, mirrors Q40):** wiring the alert into a cloud routine / cron is a checklist for Ryan, not done autonomously.
Why: the 2026-07-16 tape audit confirmed the pipe leaks silently (a full day lost 07-09, a leg dead ~24h unnoticed until a human ran an audit). GOAL.md kill-criterion #2 (missing-day <2%) and the M5 certification gate are unmeasurable without this monitor; it is the prerequisite that lets any new Phase-1 family ship onto a monitored pipe. Cheap, ungated, highest-leverage reliability fix.

### Q46 — Full-universe top-of-book sweep (GOAL.md Phase-1 M2)
Status: DONE (2026-07-17, research loop) — `collection/universe_sweep.py` built (+16 new tests: 10 `tests/test_universe_sweep.py` + 6 `tests/test_hourly_pass.py`), read-only + unauthenticated over the public `/markets?status=open` listing, NO `series_ticker` (a genuine full-universe sweep), bounded at a `MAX_CALLS=20` cap. One append-only JSONL snapshot line per open market with raw top-of-book (`yes_bid`/`yes_ask`/`no_bid`/`no_ask` parsed from Kalshi's `_dollars` strings, L90) + at-touch sizes + `last_price` + `volume`/`volume_24h` + `open_interest` + `liquidity`, tagged **`real_ask`**, `raw_sha256` page-provenance per line. Top-of-book ONLY — ZERO per-market `/orderbook` calls (no scope-creep into the L2/Phase-2 depth lane). NOT deduped across passes (correct for a BBO time series, unlike the settlement label ledger). Honest completeness: hitting the call cap with an active cursor sets `truncated=True`/`completeness_ok=False`; nothing else lowers it. Wired into `hourly_pass.py` on `UNIVERSE_SWEEP_UTC_HOURS = {0, 6, 12, 18}` with the same `_safe_call` fault-isolation as every sibling; unlike the settlement/forecast/actuals label legs, these are FRESH live BBOs so they DO fold into n_markets/n_lines. **Live run, independently re-verified against committed tape (not just the agent's self-report):** 20 calls, 20,000 lines, all `price_source_tag: real_ask`, single `capture_id`, 0 JSON parse errors, 0 missing required fields; 7,489/20k lines carry a non-zero `yes_ask`, 2,018/20k a non-zero `volume`. `pytest`: 1167 passed (1151 prior + 16 new). `invariants --full`: green (only pre-existing non-gating L25/L74 advisories); Hard Rule #3 not tripped (prices parsed from `_dollars` and stored raw, no `yes_ask`/`no_ask` arithmetic). No strategy claim, no P&L, `kb/strategies/00-index.md` untouched — collector build, two-agent verdict rule does not apply (Q44/Q45 precedent).
**STOP-level premise finding — ESCALATED to Ryan, NOT silently forced:** the live `status=open` universe is **>80,000 markets** (probed to 80 calls; the cursor was still active at 80k), NOT the ~10k the queue assumed. So the queue's “≥95% coverage in ≤20 calls” acceptance is UNMEETABLE at the ≤20-call bound: 20×1000 reaches ≤20k = **<25% coverage**, and every live pass HONESTLY reports `truncated=True`/`completeness_ok=False`. The collector's honest-partial behavior is working exactly as designed; it is the acceptance TARGET (and its 10k premise) that is broken. **Storage bombshell (GOAL.md M3, Ryan-gated):** ~890 bytes/line × 20k = **17.8 MB per capped pass** × 4/day ≈ **~71 MB/day** — already OVER the 50 MB external-storage ceiling in a SINGLE day (and full 80k-coverage would be ~1 GB/day), vastly above the queue's projected 12 MB/day (which assumed ~3 MB/pass at ~10k markets). **Dead-tail finding:** ~63% of captured open markets have `yes_ask=0` and ~90% `volume=0` (dominated by auto-generated `KXMVESPORTSMULTIGAMEEXTENDED` multi-leg series) — a cross-sectional BBO census should filter on activity/liquidity before treating a market as a real quote. **Three Ryan design calls, NONE decided here:** (a) raise the call cap (~85+ calls to exhaust >80k at 1000/page); (b) add an activity/liquidity discovery filter to shrink both the target universe AND the storage; (c) accept a bounded partial-coverage snapshot per pass (the current honest behavior). **The leg is wired but its live {0,6,12,18} cadence is effectively gated behind the storage decision** — flagged, not switched on. **Wording divergences (documented, not forced):** (1) “verbatim BBOs” are parsed `_dollars`/`_fp` strings → floats (sibling-consistent w/ sports_pairs/settlement_ledger, invariant-safe), not raw strings; (2) the coverage cross-check “against the listing's own total count” found the listing exposes NO total field (top-level keys are just `cursor`/`markets`), so coverage is asserted by clean cursor-exhaustion, with total-count coverage wired future-proof for if Kalshi ever adds it. **Run-hygiene note for Ryan:** this run hit a background-subagent race — a delegated `collector-engineer` ran concurrently with the lead's direct build and collided on the same files (duplicate test defs, a clobbered untracked module, a 3× bloated smoke tape); resolved to a single coherent state and one clean 20k-line pass, but the lesson is: never run a background collector build concurrently with direct edits to the same files. Lesson candidates for a kb-distiller pass: correct L10's “10k+” figure to >80k; the dead-tail activity-filter rule; L90 corroboration for OPEN markets; the multi-hour-gate test-collision rule.
Status update (2026-07-21, idle-run policy (c), does NOT alter the DONE verdict): a full-history liquidity census (`scripts/universe_sweep_liquidity_census.py` over `dt=2026-07-17`..`21`, 300,000 lines / 0 malformed, all `real_ask`, NO network) now feeds Ryan design-call **(b)** ["add an activity/liquidity discovery filter"] with concrete storage-saving numbers: filtering at capture time to the ACTIVITY tier (`open_interest>0 OR volume>0`) retains only **10.74% of bytes** (~71 MB/day → ~7.6 MB/day), to FILLABLE (`yes_ask>0 AND yes_ask_size>=1`) **2.89% of bytes** (~2 MB/day), to LIQUID **2.76%** — an ~89–97% cut that drops only no-offer / no-activity artifacts (**96.97%** of the census is a dead tail, **~96.9%** of it two auto-generated multi-leg series `KXMVESPORTSMULTIGAMEEXTENDED` 82.21% + `KXMVECROSSCATEGORY` 14.68%). Confirms `volume_24h` is effectively always-zero family-wide (~5/300k rows; the L96 schema defect, across the full history). **NO code/collector change to `universe_sweep` this run** — cadence + filter stay Ryan-gated. the entry gate "spread ≥ 2 fees" arithmetically guarantees non-negative double-fill P&L — the L41-
inadmissible verdicts on wider cuts carry no evidentiary weight; the real kill is the sub-tick magnitude
decomposition + the (admissible) strategy-level bootstrap. Verifier independently reproduced every
number byte-for-byte (JSON-diffed two runs, fully deterministic), proved the fee identity holds on all
445 wide-spread candidates (0 net-negative, min net = $0.0000 exactly), confirmed 0/53 depth-tape series
prefixes are `KXMVE*` (S68 exclusion moot, not violated), and built an independent alternative entry rule
(first-snapshot-at-ttc≤H, 4 horizons) — every one DEAD too, one (ttc≤6h) strategy-level CI **negative**

20 candidates share one entry timestamp — a tape-start artifact, not a temporally-spread near-close
sample; the "measured not assumed" framing of the fee identity is actually a tautology given collector
construction) — neither changes the verdict. `python3 -m pytest -q` 2547/2547 passed (producer +
verifier, independently); `scripts/invariants.py --full` all green. **Still 0 proven edges.** See
`findings/2026-08-01-q49-s68-bothside-maker-fillsim-verdict.md`.

flips; this hardens a stated CAVEAT into a statistic, not a result**). Q49's own module docstring said
its loose `turnover` fill rule "SATURATES over a multi-day hold ... that is an artifact of the proxy,
not evidence of fills" — a caveat in prose, with the three numbers that prove it (fill rate,

`saturated=True`; PRIMARY `fillable_entry` n=20, loose **20/20 = 100%**
(`loose_rule_discriminates=False`) vs strict **55%**. L250's own stated 98%-vs-42% reproduces exactly.
No CI, no P&L, no registry change — **S68 stays `dead x`**; two-agent rule N/A for the milestone class

have been dispatched regardless. 16 new tests. Open `UNENFORCED` rows **6 -> 5**. See

Mechanism (see `kb/strategies/00-index.md` S68 row + `findings/2026-08-01-q21-idea-gen-round.md`): on
2-outcome game moneyline books whose two-sided spread ≥ 2× the flat maker fee, rest BOTH a YES bid and
a NO bid; if both fill you own both sides for `yes_bid+no_bid` (mean 0.927 on the 205-event wide
population) < $1 and one settles $1 → deterministic +7.31¢ gross / +5.31¢ net of the 2¢ two-sided
maker fee. The idea-stage overround is real and clears L41 (16 game series) / L9 / L31; the EDGE is
entirely the fill model.
Milestone (one read-only probe): build a queue-aware BOTH-sides-fill maker sim over
`tape/orderbook_depth/`'s `yes_bids`/`no_bids` price-time-priority ladders (the S6/S19/S21/S23
L2-queue methodology, L39-free — never a candle-through print), joined ex-post to
`tape/settlement_ledger/` `broker_truth` (L50). For each wide-spread (yes-spread ≥ 2¢) genuinely-two-
sided game book, simulate resting BOTH bids with an EXPLICIT adverse-selection model (the side that
fills is disproportionately the side about to lose — this is the whole question), require BOTH fills
before booking the overround, charge the flat 1¢ maker fee PER filled leg via `core.pricing` (never
hand-rolled, L18/L30), settle at `broker_truth`. Block-bootstrap by GAME-SERIES (L6/L41, the 16
series are the independent units — strikes/games within a series are correlated draws). Route through
`bootstrap_verdict_admissible` + `clears_tick_magnitude`. Two-agent rule: producer (edge-prober) +
independent `verifier` CONFIRM before any registry flip.
Binding gates: (1) fillable object is `real_bid`; `broker_truth` settlement gates the payout, never a
fill. (2) BOTH bids must fill for the overround — a single-side fill is a directional position, not the
capture (the single-side cuts already straddle zero / are a NO-base-rate artifact). (3) adverse
selection must be modeled, not assumed away — an optimistic guaranteed-both-fill number reproduces the
+5.31¢ and proves nothing (L5). (4) net of the maker fee via `core/pricing.py`.
Kill: fill rate below the S19 ~0.45% floor / the realized-both-fill population's overround ≤ 0 once
adverse selection is charged / block-boot CI ≤ 0 / population below the 10-game-series floor after the
queue gate. Honest expectation: KILL on adverse selection (the S6/S13/S14/S23 maker fill-wall applied
to a two-sided book) — but the overround is deterministic and the population clears every structural
floor, so it earns one real probe rather than a pre-kill.

+$0.0524, CI [-$0.0250,+$0.1361], 6 units — same verdict. **All binding gates held:** 26/26
fills trace to a `broker_truth` `trade_id` (the predicate reads a print or returns False, so a
synthesised fill cannot occur); NO queue-position or time-to-fill number is computed anywhere
and the report's key set is test-asserted free of them; interval coverage is reported beside
every fill rate on both branches. **Why n=7:** 145 of the day's 165 sports intervals die
because the market is still `active` — 49 of 60 sampled sports markets are games scheduled
2026-08-04..08-09. ZERO intervals were lost to a missing settlement record, a non-binary
result (L52), a one-sided book, or a post-close entry. The spec's kill conditions read
literally as a kill, but the L41 gate fires FIRST and an inadmissible CI is not a verdict, so
this run records DATA-INADEQUATE and explicitly declines to convert a 7-unit straddle into a
kill; S13/S23/S29 keep the status they already had.
**FIRST RESULT: milestone 1 read the tape BACKWARDS (new lesson L279).** `taker_book_side` is
NOT "the side of the BOOK the taker crossed into" — it names the side the TAKER'S OWN order
sat on, so a `bid` taker BUYS (lifting a resting offer) and an `ask` taker SELLS (hitting a
resting bid). On prints within 15 min of their reference snapshot: `bid` prints execute at/above
the best ask **86.8%** (n=151), `ask` prints at/below the best bid **83.3%** (n=30), decaying
monotonically to 84.6%/70.4% as the join window widens to <=60min/any age. The SAME tape read
milestone 1's way gives 27.5% fill and mean **-$0.066**; read correctly, 65.0% and **+$0.045**
— the point estimate changes SIGN. No captured record changed (the collector stores the field
verbatim); the collector docstring is corrected in place and the milestone-1 finding is
ANNOTATED, not rewritten. Fill-rate asymmetry is the run's one robust observation and follows
from the correction: YES-bid 45.0% vs NO-bid 85.0%, because taker flow is ~80% buying.
**Two-agent status: PROVISIONAL.** No `verifier` subagent was dispatchable (no `Task` tool in
context — as on Q19/Q49/Q50 and milestone 1). The sanctioned fallback ran instead: a second
INDEPENDENT code path (own reader, own Decimal round-up fee vs the probe's `math.ceil`, own
grouping, own bootstrap, seed 20260804) reading ONLY `reports/q51_maker_fillsim_rows.jsonl` and
never importing the probe — 40/40 rows, **0 P&L mismatches, 0 untraced fills, 0 price-tag
violations**, mean +$0.04450, 7 units, 4 opposing, CI [-$0.0212,+$0.1181], same verdict. That
is a redundancy check, NOT a verifier, and it is honest about its limit: it could not have
caught the orientation error (it would have inherited the misreading) — only the tape did. No
row in `kb/strategies/00-index.md` moves. See
`findings/2026-08-04-q51-maker-fillsim-milestone2.md`.

**Milestone 3 (TODO — now a one-command re-pull, not a collection campaign):** re-pull
`tape/q51_settlement_cache/settlement.json` for the SAME 60 tickers once the 2026-08-04..08-09

### Q53 — `check_monotonicity`'s nesting premise: a shared `event_ticker` is not a strike ladder (L291)
Status: TODO (added 2026-08-06, research loop IDLE RUN policy (a), from the L288->L290 guard build).
NOT a probe and NOT verdict-class as filed: it is a correctness repair to the repo's oldest live
scanner, `scripts/anomaly_sweep.py::check_monotonicity`, plus the S3/S15 verdict that becomes
possible once the scanner stops emitting false positives.
**The defect (measured, L291).** After the L290 fillability guard removes the 43,025 `$0.00`-leg
records, **13 of 43,038** committed anomalies survive — and all 13 pair two DIFFERENT SUBJECTS
under one `event_ticker` (two tennis players' game spreads, two batters' props, three cities'
rain markets), which the check sorts by `floor_strike`/`cap_strike` as if they were rungs of one
ladder. Buying YES(subject A) + NO(subject B) is a naked directional bet, never a guaranteed
>= $1 payout. Evidence: `findings/2026-08-06-anomaly-sweep-fillability-guard.md`, and
`tape/universe_sweep/` titles showing one event holding both "Will A win by >= 2.5 more games
than B?" and "Will B win by >= 1.5 more games than A?".
**Milestones.** (1) Build a SUBJECT-IDENTITY test for a candidate nested pair and validate it
against a real ladder corpus — `tape/econ_prints/`, `tape/weather_books/`, `tape/crypto_hourly/`
all carry genuine nested ladders with real tickers, and `tape/universe_sweep/` carries titles for
the multi-subject counterexamples; report BOTH error rates (refusing a genuine ladder is as bad
as admitting a cross-subject pair). A ticker-suffix heuristic alone is the shortcut Q1's own
build note warns against — prefer a structural confirmation (title/subtitle subject match, or
the ladder's own strike-grammar), and say plainly which the implementation actually uses.
(2) Wire it into `check_monotonicity` behind the same counted-refusal discipline the L290 guard
uses (a new refusal key, persisted, additive to `anomaly_sweep.v1`), and update
`tests/test_anomaly_sweep.py::test_acceptance_no_survivor_remains_once_the_nesting_premise_is_ENFORCED`
in the SAME commit — that pin exists to go to zero. (Citation repaired 2026-08-06 per L205 when
this milestone landed and renamed the pin; it was written as
`test_acceptance_every_survivor_is_a_cross_entity_pair_not_a_nested_ladder`.) (3) ONLY THEN is an S3/S15 verdict on the
table: 26 committed capture-days with zero verified fillable arbs is a frequency observation,
and turning it into a kill requires the two-agent rule (producer + independent `verifier`).
**Not blocked on anything.** Offline-testable end to end over committed tape; no network, no
credentials, no execution lane.
Status: MILESTONES 1-2 DONE, MILESTONE 3 DELIVERED AS A **PROVISIONAL DATA-ADEQUACY VERDICT**
(2026-08-06, research loop, main-context build — the harness exposed no `Task`/subagent tool, so
no independent `verifier` was dispatchable and NO registry status was flipped; the L287/L288/
L290/L291 precedent). **(1) Built `core/subject_identity.py`** — three-valued
(`PROVEN_SAME_SUBJECT` / `DIFFERENT_SUBJECT` / `UNVERIFIABLE`, the last two both REFUSALS at the
call site, because nesting must be proven and not merely un-disproven). It reads the market's own
`title`/`subtitle`/`yes_sub_title` anchored to its own `floor_strike`/`cap_strike` and parses **no
ticker suffix at all**; verdict = text-SKELETON equality (which is what discriminates — subjects
differ in WORDS) AND every differing numeric token explainable by a SHARED offset
`a_token == a_strike + d`, `b_token == b_strike + d`. The offset is real and non-zero on tape
(`KXHIGHNY-...-T96` publishes `97° or above`, **+1**; `KXTEMPNYCH-...-T81.99` publishes
`82° or above`, **+0.01**; `KXCPICORE` publishes `0.3` for `floor_strike 0.3`, **0**) — a
label==strike rule would refuse EVERY weather ladder on committed tape, the KXFEDDECISION
'>25bps as 26' trap one family over. **Both error rates, closed window `dt <= 2026-08-04`,
exhaustive (0 classes sampled), via `scripts/subject_identity_corpus_audit.py` ->
`reports/subject_identity_corpus_audit.json`: FALSE-REFUSE 0 / 34,334** genuine-ladder
monotonicity-shaped pairs (econ_prints 2,348/0, weather_books 31,986/0; crypto_hourly contributes
0 pairs BY CONSTRUCTION — one `greater` + one `less` per event — reported, not hidden in a total)
and **FALSE-ADMIT 0 / 2,364** pairs a ground-truth player-name regex (computed independently of
the predicate) labels cross-subject, with **0 / 151** false refusals of the genuine within-player
ladders sitting in the SAME events. Platform-wide over 1,190,426 `tape/universe_sweep/`
within-event pairs: 932,965 (78.37%) decided-refuse, **15** decided-admit — all 15 verified
CORRECT (`KXATPGTOTAL` total-games rungs of one match) — 257,446 (21.63%) INDETERMINATE because
that family persists no strike fields, a corpus limit enumerated (24,094 skeletons, dominated by
`KXMVE*` parlays that carry no `strike_type` and by genuine `KXGOLDH`/`KXSILVERH`/`KXWTIH`
ladders) rather than assumed away. The measurement forced a design change: scoring a whole MECE
ladder on the sub-title refuses **880/1,591 (55.3%)** genuine single-city weather ladders, since
one city's ladder carries three sub-title GRAMMARS — hence `DESCRIPTIVE_FIELDS` (same
`strike_type`) vs `SUBJECT_FIELDS_CROSS_STRIKE_TYPE` (title only, cross-type). **(2) Wired** into
`check_monotonicity` AND `check_bracket_arb` behind L290's counted-refusal discipline: two new
keys `n_cross_subject_pair_refusals` / `n_subject_unverifiable_refusals` (additive to
`anomaly_sweep.v1`, no existing field changed, kept SEPARATE so 'provably different things' can
never be misread as 'could not tell'), plus a new `subject_identity_reason` on every flagged
anomaly so a future replay can audit why a premise was accepted. The guard runs LAST in
`check_monotonicity` so the live ledger's funnel matches the published replay exactly. Committed
replay now runs **43,038 -> 43,025 unbuyable -> 13 -> 0**, and
the pin formerly named `test_acceptance_every_survivor_is_a_cross_entity_pair_not_a_nested_ladder`
(bare name on purpose — it no longer exists, so a node-id citation here would dangle, L205) was
replaced in the SAME commit by
`tests/test_anomaly_sweep.py::test_acceptance_no_survivor_remains_once_the_nesting_premise_is_ENFORCED` (the 6 named pairs
are retained beside it as the historical population). Read the mechanism honestly: a committed
anomaly record persists only tickers, so the replay CANNOT prove subject identity from tape and
all 13 are refused as `UNVERIFIABLE` — the discrimination proof is fixture-side and corpus-side.
**(3) Milestone 3 — S3/S15 DATA-ADEQUACY verdict, PROVISIONAL, no registry flip.** Exposure over
26 capture-days / 248 passes: 4,908,300 market-observations, 2,210 monotonicity group-checks, 0
verified fillable arbs -> rule-of-three 95% bound <= 3/26 = **0.115 per capture-day**;

## Retro amendments — proposed 2026-07-05, ADOPTED 2026-07-10 (PR #18 merged)

Drafted by the weekly retro run from that week's "Log of runs". **Adopted** — Ryan merged
PR #18 on 2026-07-10T19:55:32Z, so all 3 items below are now binding protocol, not proposals.
This run (2026-07-11) already followed #1 (mandatory `git reset --hard origin/main` before
the step 0b diff) and #2 (no more `git push origin --delete` retries) and applied #3 (PR #4
is 8 days old, flagged `Priority: high` in this run's phone note). Nothing here relaxed an
invariant or a Stop rule, deleted or reordered a queue item, or touched source code.

1. **Step 0b clarification — reset local `main` before diffing stranded branches.** On
   2026-07-05T05:19Z the research run found its sandbox's local `main` ref was ~2 days stale,
   which made every `tape/hourly-*` branch look like it carried far more missing lines than it
   actually did (including in files the collector never touches) — caught before it produced
   a bad commit, but only because that run happened to check. Proposed addition to step 0b:
   run `git fetch origin main && git reset --hard origin/main` (or equivalent) immediately
   before diffing any `tape/hourly-*` branch against `main`, every run, not only when a diff
   looks suspicious.

2. **Step 0b — stop retrying the branch-delete that always fails.** Every research run since
   2026-07-03 (at least 5 runs, per the log below) has attempted `git push origin --delete` on
   fully-reconciled `tape/hourly-*` branches, and every single attempt has failed with the same
   documented cloud-session permission boundary. Proposed: stop attempting the delete each run
   — it costs a tool call and a log sentence for a guaranteed no-op — and just note
   reconciled-but-undeleted branches once per run instead. Separately, flagging for Ryan: if
   the stale branches should actually get cleaned up, the cloud GitHub App/token would need
   branch-delete scope added. That's a one-time permissions change only Ryan can make; no loop
   run can fix it from inside the sandbox.

3. **New — stuck-PR escalation after 5+ days with no owner action.** PR #4 (Q1's odds-api leg)
   has been open since 2026-07-03 waiting on Ryan to paste `ODDS_API_KEY` into the environment
   — at least 6 research runs now have silently re-noted "skipped Q1, unrelated" without ever
   escalating. Proposed: if an open PR has sat more than 5 days blocked purely on a Ryan-side
   action (a key, a decision, a merge) with no new activity, that run's ntfy phone note should
   use `Priority: high` (instead of the default) and name the specific blocking action once,
   so a stuck item doesn't stay silent indefinitely.
